description: Use this to add clothes to the user's wardrobe so a character can wear them. Give a picture (image_url: any picture's own address, a shop's product page, or a URL from upload_media; or image_base64) or a description. A product page is read for its product picture, but many shops (Amazon, Zara, H&M, eBay ...) don't allow automatic reading or show no product picture: the tool then says the page can't be read and what to do. Ask the user for the picture's own address (right-click the picture, Copy image address) or the picture itself, or, if you can browse, open the page yourself and pass the product picture's address. mode: photo (default for a picture: someone wears it and the clothes are taken out onto an invisible mannequin; charged at the image model's usual price, like generate_image), clean (the picture shows only the clothes: used as it is, free) or text (designed from the description, the model's usual price). note says what to take when a photo shows more ("only the leather jacket"). The picture takes about a minute: call get_wardrobe_item with the returned id until it is ready, then write its @handle next to a character in generate_image or generate_video.

description.description: The clothes in words, to design them (mode text). A link inside is read like image_url.

fit.description: Optional: who it is cut for (judged from the picture otherwise).

image_base64.description: The picture as base64 or a data URL, when you have the file.

image_url.description: A picture's own address, a shop's product page (read for its product picture), one of the user's BudgetPixel picture links, or a URL from upload_media.

mode.description: photo: someone wears it, the clothes are taken out onto an invisible mannequin (default for a picture). clean: the picture shows only the clothes, used as it is (free). text: designed from the description.

model.description: Optional: the image model that makes the picture for photo and text (default nano-banana-2.1).

name.description: Optional: a name (one is written for it otherwise).

note.description: With a photo: what to take when it shows more, e.g. "only the leather jacket".

name: add_wardrobe_item
title: Add Wardrobe Item
